name: How much contingency should I include for a Los Angeles remodel?

mainEntity.name: What contingency budget is appropriate for a luxury home remodel in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What contingency budget is appropriate for a luxury home remodel in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is one of the most overlooked parts of a remodel budget, yet it is critical for Los Angeles projects. A reasonable contingency depends on project risk. A newer home with a well-defined scope may need a smaller reserve, while an older home, hillside property, or major renovation with uncertain conditions may require more. For luxury remodels, contingency should be separated from allowances. Allowances cover known categories like fixtures or finishes that have not yet been fully selected. Contingency covers unknowns, such as hidden framing issues, unexpected structural work, or scope changes that arise during construction. The most useful approach is to set contingency early, then track it carefully during design and construction. If the budget is tight, do not hide contingency inside other line items. That creates false confidence. A transparent contingency gives you flexibility when surprises appear. In Los Angeles, where many homes are older and project complexity can increase quickly, a stronger contingency plan can save the project. Ask your builder to explain what risks the contingency is meant to cover and when it can be released. That keeps the budget honest and reduces stress later in the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency range for a Los Angeles remodel is often 10% to 20%, with higher reserves for older homes, unknown site conditions, or extensive design changes. The more incomplete the design or the older the home, the larger the contingency should be. Contingency should be separate from allowances and should not be treated as extra spending money.
